note: THE PAID-EVENT COPY, THE QR CODE, THE MISSING CRM ACTIVITY, AND A DEAD CONTROL. Six founder reports against the paid-event flow THE-351 and THE-355 built, two of them about money and one about a claim Harvest cannot stand behind. ONE - THE DOOR GUARANTEE IS DELETED FROM EVERY ATTENDEE SURFACE. "'Bring this ticket either way - you will not be turned away at the door.' this should be deleted. there is no way for us to know what each church is doing. or ministry." It stood on four surfaces (the member's waiting note, the public How-to-pay block, the public no-links state, the public claimed state) and in the registration email, and nothing softer replaced it: a hedge would be the same unknowable claim with a qualifier. THE BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED - check-in still never blocks on payment, the Check In control is still gated on `status === 'confirmed'` alone, and the ADMIN disclaimer still says an unpaid ticket is let in, because that sentence is about HARVEST'S OWN software, which is knowable and is what an admin needs before pricing an event. TWO - THE "I'VE PAID" DISCLAIMER IS REWRITTEN. It read "This only tells the church to go and look. It settles nothing on its own and it does not change what you owe." It now reads "This does not confirm payment. It asks {tenant} to look for it in their own account." It keeps the one fact it exists for - the press confirms nothing - names the tenant, and drops the debt line, which reads as collection over a gift. The public variant keeps its third sentence, "Keep the email with your ticket code", because a logged-out registrant cannot come back to that screen. THREE - NO QR CODE UNTIL THE PAYMENT IS CONFIRMED. "the user should not have the qr code unless his payment has been confirmed." The gate is the ABSENCE OF A CONFIRMATION, not the presence of a price, so a FREE ticket - which has no payment to confirm - is completely unaffected and still renders its QR immediately, asserted at both spellings including a row from before the payment field existed. The ticket CODE is withheld with the QR on the member's dialog, because the code IS the QR's payload and printing it beside a withheld QR is the same token in text; the code STAYS on the public success screen and in the email, which are the only record a logged-out registrant will ever hold. What stands in the QR's place says the registration is complete and the place is held, so an absent QR cannot read as a failed registration. No migration: the state is derived from fields the registration already carries. FOUR - THE TENANT'S NAME, NEVER "THE CHURCH". "instead of 'the church', say the name of the ministry. not all tenants are churches." Five confirmed strings plus the claim help, the failed-press notice and two public headings became builders over the tenant name, resolved through ONE `tenantLabel` so two surfaces cannot describe the same missing name differently. The fallback is `the event organizer` - true of a church, a ministry and a crusade host alike, never "Harvest", which is the one word that must not stand where the party that collects and decides goes. FIVE - the waiting note lost both halves of the sentence the founder quoted; what remains is one line naming who was asked and what for. SIX - A CONFIRMED PAYMENT NOW WRITES A CRM ACTIVITY. "in crm it doesnt show that i have paid for an event after i confirmed but it appears in the accounting." The confirm route wrote the invoice through `recordManualDonation` and nothing else. It now also writes a DONATION activity in THE-350'S EXACT SHAPE - `amount: null` plus `invoiceId`, with `invoiceAmountCents` as a display mirror in cents under a name nothing in this repository sums - so the gift cannot be counted twice and `totalDonated` cannot double. It runs LAST and is best-effort: a failed timeline write cannot un-confirm a gift that landed. Idempotence is phase 1's, unchanged: two taps produce one invoice and one activity. The contact is matched by EMAIL within the tenant, one single-field query filtered in memory so no composite index is needed; a registrant with no contact row gets no activity and NO contact is minted, because populating the CRM from a public event form and spending a tenant's contact capacity is not this route's decision. `totalDonated` is untouched. SEVEN - the `← Notes` control is NOT removed. STOP condition 6, reported: it is not dead. It carries `onClick={closeEditor}`, which saves and awaits before leaving, and four existing tests drive it. The ticket's premise for removing it - that the breadcrumb already does the job - is false: the breadcrumb's root crumb is an inert span. Below `lg` the tree is off screen while a note is open and in focus mode the app header and bottom nav are both hidden, so on a phone this control is the ONLY exit from the editor. It looks like it does nothing on the DESKTOP the founder is using because the tree is already beside the editor there, so there is nowhere to go back to. AdminDocs.tsx is byte-identical. EIGHT - the partnership empty state became one button; see the Profile.tsx entry in the settings freeze register, which is where that file is pinned. No token, no component and no dependency was added; `firestore.rules`, `firestore.indexes.json`, `functions/` and `layout.tsx` are byte-identical and no firestore.rules digest is recorded here.

entries.why: THE ATTENDEE COPY, REWRITTEN, AND THE TENANT RESOLVER THAT HOLDS IT TOGETHER. The door guarantee is deleted from `memberClaimedBody`, `publicPayBody`, `publicNoLinksBody` and `publicClaimedBody`, and the 'Harvest has not checked anything and cannot' clause with it - the founder asked for both halves of that sentence to go, and nothing softer stands in their place. `MEMBER_CLAIM_HELP` and `PUBLIC_CLAIM_HELP` became `memberClaimHelp`/`publicClaimHelp`, keeping the premise (the press does not confirm payment) and dropping the debt line. Six constants that said 'the church' became builders over the tenant name: `memberClaimedBadge`, `memberConfirmedBadge`, `memberClaimedTitle`, `memberClaimFailed`, `publicNoLinksTitle` and `publicClaimedTitle`. `tenantLabel` and `TENANT_NAME_FALLBACK` are new and are the ONE place a missing name is resolved, so the ticket dialog and the public page cannot answer it differently; the fallback is 'the event organizer', never 'Harvest'. `TICKET_QR_WAITING_TITLE` and `ticketQrWaitingBody` are new and are what stands where a withheld QR was, on all three surfaces that withhold one. ADMIN COPY IS UNTOUCHED and stays out of scope by the ticket's own words: `CREATION_DISCLAIMER_BODY` still tells the admin an unpaid ticket is let in, which is a statement about Harvest's own check-in and is what this ticket must not change, and the inbox still says Harvest has checked nothing to the admin who is about to check. No forbidden claim phrase is introduced at either a real tenant name or a missing one.

NO QR ON A PAID TICKET NOBODY HAS CONFIRMED, AND THE TENANT NAMED IN EVERY STATE. `TicketModal` computes `awaitingPayment` from the ticket's own payment state - true only for `unpaid` and `claimed` - and while it holds, the QR is not generated at all (not merely hidden), the ticket code is not printed, and 'Present this at the door' does not render, because there is nothing to present. An Alert stands in their place carrying 'Your place is held' and the reason, so the absence cannot read as a failed registration; `alert` is the primitive this screen already uses for a standing notice about the state of a record and it carries role=alert. A FREE ticket takes the false branch - `?? 'free'` also covers a row from before the payment field existed - and is completely unaffected. `TicketPaymentPanel` and `TicketModal` take `tenantName` instead of `churchName`, and the local `|| 'the church'` fallback is REMOVED: the raw value goes to the copy functions, every one of which resolves it through `tenantLabel`, so this screen and the public page cannot disagree about a missing name. No colour, no token and no height is minted; the claim button and its help are unchanged apart from the wording they render.

THE PUBLIC SUCCESS SCREEN STOPS CALLING AN UNCONFIRMED TICKET A DOOR PASS. For a priced registration - `paymentReference` present and not waitlisted, which on this screen is by construction unconfirmed - 'Show this code at the door:' is replaced by the same 'Your place is held' wording the member's dialog uses. THE CODE ITSELF STAYS HERE, deliberately and differently from the in-app ticket: a logged-out registrant can never come back to this render, it and the email are the only record they will hold, and the claim copy tells them to keep it; a code is not a scannable ticket and check-in never blocks on payment. The claimed heading, the no-links heading, the claim help and the failed-press notice now name the tenant instead of 'the church', and the door guarantee is gone from the How-to-pay block and the no-links state. The claim control, its token, the discount flow, the waitlist and the Stripe-return gate are untouched.

THE REGISTRATION EMAIL LOSES THE DOOR PROMISE AND, FOR A PAID TICKET, THE QR. The pay note's last sentence - 'Bring this ticket either way - you will not be turned away at the door' - is deleted. The QR block is now gated on `owesManualPayment`, the same condition the pay note is built on rather than a fresh `amount > 0`, so a waitlisted or discounted-to-zero seat cannot trip it: a FREE ticket still embeds its QR image exactly as before, and a paid one carries the 'Your place is held' wording instead, because this send happens seconds after registration and the payment is unconfirmed by construction. THE TICKET CODE STAYS IN THE EMAIL - it is the only record a logged-out registrant will ever hold, the claim copy tells them to keep it, and a code is not a scannable ticket. The existing 'Registered: <event>' CRM activity, the waitlist, discount codes, ticket-type capacity and the response shape are all unchanged.

A CONFIRMED EVENT PAYMENT NOW REACHES THE CRM, IN THE SHAPE THAT CANNOT DOUBLE-COUNT IT. A new phase 3c writes a DONATION activity on the contact after the invoice and the stamp have landed. It follows THE-350's shape byte for byte: `amount: null` so nothing that sums `contactActivities.amount` - the field the Stripe webhook writes in DOLLARS - can pick the gift up a second time, `invoiceId` pointing at the money, and `invoiceAmountCents` as a display mirror in cents under a name no money reader in this repository touches. The description names the event and matches the invoice's. The contact is found by ONE single-field email query with the tenant filtered in memory - the same shape `/api/event-registration/submit` already uses - so no composite index is needed and `firestore.indexes.json`, which `deploy-rules.yml` does not deploy, stays untouched. A registrant with no contact row gets no activity and no contact is created: minting one would populate the CRM from the public event form and spend the tenant's contact capacity without anybody asking. `totalDonated` is not written, because it is a client-maintained read-modify-write that a server-side bump would race. IDEMPOTENCE IS PHASE 1'S AND IS UNCHANGED - a second press finds `paymentInvoiceId` and returns before phase 2, so two taps produce one invoice AND one activity - and `recordManualDonation` is still the only money writer. The activity is best-effort and logged, never thrown, so a failed timeline write cannot un-confirm a gift that is already recorded. Both collections it now reaches, `contacts` and `contactActivities`, are already enumerated by `member-erasure.ts` and `member-export.ts`, including the donation-activity retention carve-out, so no GDPR path learns anything new.

ONE LINE, BECAUSE A CONSTANT BECAME A BUILDER. `MEMBER_CLAIM_FAILED` said 'the church has not been told' and is now `memberClaimFailed(tenantName)`, so this route calls it with `null`: it holds a tenantId, not a tenant NAME, and a document read on the failure path to fetch one would be a second way to fail while already failing. `tenantLabel`'s fallback is exactly what that case is for, and the surfaces that DO hold the name render their own copy of the sentence with it interpolated. Nothing about the route's behaviour, its permission gate, its transaction or its response shape changed.

THE SAME ONE LINE AS THE AUTHENTICATED CLAIM ROUTE, AND NOTHING ELSE. `MEMBER_CLAIM_FAILED` became `memberClaimFailed(null)` for the reason recorded on that route: this handler has a tenantId and no tenant name, and a read on the failure path is a second failure. THE SECURITY SHAPE IS UNTOUCHED AND IS ASSERTED AS A NO-REGRESSION: the request body still carries a 256-bit token and NO registration id, and the row is still selected BY that token rather than validated against a client-supplied id, so no request can name somebody else's seat.

ONE APPENDED LINE AND ONE INCREMENTED COUNT, exactly as the eleven tickets before this one did. THE-359 adds a suite that pins the `firestore.rules` digest, so section 5's exact floor moves from 71 to 72 and `RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE` gains a row naming the suite and, in the comment above it, everything that suite asserts. THE FLOOR IS RAISED, NEVER LOWERED, and no existing row is edited, reordered or removed: the claim section 5 makes - that no suite ever quietly STOPS pinning a file which auto-deploys to production with no emulator tests - is strictly stronger afterwards. Nothing else in this file changed: no accepted digest was substituted, no assertion was added, removed or loosened, and the pre-migration BEFORE inventory is untouched.
